title: Vectors
overview: Revise 3D lines, dot product, angles/intersections. This guide turns the current syllabus outcomes into a connected revision sequence: learn the ideas, practise the method, then use the recall cards and checklist to diagnose what still needs work.
syllabusPoints: Use 2D and 3D position, displacement and unit vectors.
Write and interpret r=a+λb for a straight line.
Determine whether two lines are parallel, intersecting or skew.
Use the scalar product to find angles and perpendicular projections.

definitions.definition: The vector from the origin to a point.
Any non-zero vector parallel to a line.
Non-parallel lines in 3D that do not intersect.

sections.title: Vector operations
content: For a=(a₁,a₂,a₃), |a|=√(a₁²+a₂²+a₃²) and the unit vector in its direction is a/|a|. If A and B have position vectors a and b, then AB=b−a and the midpoint is (a+b)/2.
bullets: A displacement vector has direction; distance is its magnitude.
Use exact radicals unless a decimal is requested.

sections.title: Vector equations of lines
content: The line through point A with position vector a and direction b is r=a+λb. Through A and B, use direction b−a. Direction vectors can be scalar multiples and still describe parallel lines.
bullets: The parameter is a scalar, not a vector component.
Read a point from the fixed vector and direction from the coefficient of λ.

sections.title: Intersections and skew lines
content: Equate the x, y and z components of two line equations. Solve two equations for the two parameters, then test the third. If it fails, non-parallel lines are skew; if directions are multiples, test whether a point lies on both lines.
bullets: Report the point of intersection, not only parameter values.

sections.title: Scalar products and perpendicularity
content: Compute a·b=a₁b₁+a₂b₂+a₃b₃. Perpendicular vectors have dot product 0. For an angle use cosθ=(a·b)/(|a||b|); for the acute angle between lines, reverse a direction if necessary or use |a·b|.
bullets: A foot of a perpendicular lies on the line and its displacement to the external point has zero dot product with the line direction.
Shortest distance between skew lines is outside this syllabus.

examTips: Use different parameter letters for different lines.
For line angles, state whether the question wants the acute angle or a directed angle.
Show the mathematical setup and exact working before the final rounded answer; unsupported calculator output may not earn method marks.
commonMistakes: Assuming two non-parallel 3D lines must intersect.
Solving only two components and skipping the third.
Using position vectors instead of direction vectors in the angle formula.

quickRecall.question: How do you form AB from position vectors?
How do you distinguish intersecting and skew lines?
quickRecall.answer: Solve two component equations for the parameters and check the third; failure for non-parallel lines means skew.

quickRecall.question: How is the foot from P to r=a+λb found?
quickRecall.answer: Let Q=a+λb and solve (P−Q)·b=0 for λ.
